narr: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona lead to flash flooding across the area.
ev: Heavy rain over the Museum Fire scar (2019) produce significant flooding down Spruce Wash and into north central Flagstaff and down into the Rio de Flag on the south and southeast Flagstaff. The flood water first entered developed area around 1245 PM with trees, logs, and other debris 60-70 feet wide over topping a road about 2.5 - 3 feet deep. The flood waters were over 9 feet deep in some channeled areas through the forest. Many roads were flooded and closed. The flood barriers were overtopped in some places.
The river gauge on Dry Beaver Creek near The Village of Oak Creek rose 4.5 feet. Downstream, Dry Beaver Creek rose 4.4 feet between 430 PM and 530 PM MST.
The Wet Beaver Creek gauge near Montezuma Castle showed a 2.7 foot rise between 830 PM and 1045 PM.

Heavy rain over the Fort Valley Trail System (2-3 inches in an hour) caused flash flooding through some yards north of Highway 180, the Rio de Flag in the Cheshire Subdivision (crossed two roads--first time in at least 27 years)m and all the way through Flagstaff.
Bright Angel Creek rose 6 feet at Phantom Ranch.
The Little Colorado River gauge near Cameron (LCCA3) showed a 2.9 foot rise between 815 PM and 1100 PM MST.
